articleTitle: Theory of an FIR Gas Laser
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A rate equation model for an optically pumped FIR gas laser is proposed. The gain expression includes saturation effects due to both pump power and FIR intensity. A criterion for positive gain is derived, and the role of velocity cross-relaxation examined.

articleTitle: Compact Waveguide Lasers in the Submillimeter and Millimeter Wave Regions
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Performances, for example, dependency on size and gas pressure, of metallic waveguide for far-infrared molecular lasers were studied. Compact, highly efficient, optically pumped waveguide lasers in the submillimeter and millimeter wave regions have been developed.

articleTitle: High Resolution Far Infrared Fourier Transform Spectrometry of Gases
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Techniques used at the National Physical Laboratory to study the absorption spectra of gases at a resolution of 0.05 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> in the 10 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> to 40 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> spectral region are described. New measurements on CO, N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, NO, SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>S, H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, HNO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> are shown and discussed.

articleTitle: FIR Waveguide Laser Performance in the 40μm-lmm Spectral Region
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The design of a cw compact FIR waveguide laser operating in the 40μm-lmm spectral region is described. A metallic waveguide with internal mirrors is essential for efficient operation at wavelengths greater than 500μm. Performance data are discussed.

articleTitle: A Fast, Sensitive GaAs Photoconductor System with a Cryogenic Preamplifier
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A sensitive far-infrared (100–400 μm) detector system is described consisting of a liquid-helium cooled GaAs photoconductor, cryogenic preamplifier, and room-temperature post amplifier. The system bandwidth is 1 Hz to 30 MHz, ten times greater than for InSb hot electron bolometers.

articleTitle: CW 337 μm HCN Laser Gain Saturation, Emission Line-Shape and Power
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The gain saturation of a 337 μm HCN laser is shown to be homogeneous. Dependence of gain and saturation intensity on tube radius and gas temperature leads to the design of a compact, clean running laser.

articleTitle: Low-Mode Low-Loss Waveguides and Open-Resonator Techniques at Submillimeter Wavelengths
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A modified form of H-guide is investigated theoretically and experimentally. Attenuations < 1 dB/m are predicted. Guide characteristics are verified at 8 mm wavelength, and guide attenuation of 8 dB/m achieved at 1/3 mm wavelength. Open-resonator characteristics are investigated at 337 um using a HCN laser. Resonance spectra agree with theoretical predictions and Q factors up to 8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> achieved. Dielectric permittivity and loss-tangent values are obtainable from spectra changes. This work sponsored by United Kingdom National Physical Laboratory.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Optical Instrumentation for Sub-Millimetre Astronomy
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Principles of microwave antenna design have been extended to sub-millimetre telescope and spectrometer optics. The results are systems with specially shaped reflectors, comprising two elements for radiometry and three elements for use with Michelson interferometers.

articleTitle: A Heterodyne Detection Scheme for Coherent HCN Laser Scattering from Waves and Fluctuations in Thermonuclear Plasmas
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Coherent HCN-Laser Scattering can be used as a diagnostic for waves and fluctuations in Tokamak- and Stellarator-type plasmas. Conditions for measuring the scattered light and a resulting heterodyne detection system are described.

articleTitle: Measurement of Atmospheric Attenuation at 1.3 and 0.87 mm with a Harmonic Mixing Radiometer
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The atmospheric attenuation at 1.3 and 0.87 mm was measured above Mount Hamilton, California in the period December 5 to December 9, 1973. The measured value of the zenith attenuation varied from 1 to 5 dB at 1.3 mm over this 5 day period, and was 2.5 dB at 0.87 mm on December 9, 1973. The total beamwidth of the 120” Lick Observatory telescope used in the Coudé configuration was measured to be 3' at 1.3 mm.

articleTitle: Plasma Modulation of an HCN Gas Laser
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A transient plasma is located within the Fabry-Perot resonator of a dc hydrogen cyanide laser. Plasma tuning sweeps the resonator modes through the emission line of the HCN molecules and produces pulses of far-infrared output radiation. Pulse production by hydrogen, nitrogen, helium and argon pulsed plasmas is discussed.

articleTitle: The Current Role and Future Prospects of Pyroelectric Coherent Radiation Detectors
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Theoretical estimates are presented of the limiting performance which might be achieved in the heterodyne mode with currently available pyroelectric materials over a range of intermediate frequencies. Experimental measurements on Triglycine Sulphate detectors have yielded a noise equivalent power at 10.6 μm of 2 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−15</sup> WHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, at 337 μm of 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−12</sup> WHz and at 3cm of 8 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−13</sup> WHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> with intermediate frequencies of 20 kHz, 800 Hz and 1 kHz respectively.

articleTitle: “Submillimeter-Wave Solar Brightness Temperature Measured with a Balloon-Borne Lamellar-Grating Interferometer”
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The solar brightness temperature was measured in the spectral region between 180 μm and 500 μm wavelength with a balloon-borne lamellar-grating interferometer. The result is in good agreement with the HSRA-model.

articleTitle: A Far Infrared Bolometer at 0.10 °K
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The performance of a Ge bolometer cooled to 0.10°K is discussed. A detector responsivity of 1.1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> V W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> and NEP of 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−16</sup> W Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">− 1/2</sup> are expected. A single-cycle He dilution refrigerator with no moving parts is also described.

articleTitle: Present Status of the Applications of Pyroelectricity to the Detection of Far Infrared Radiations
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The best detectivity obtained at room temperature is D∗ = 6 • 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">#x00BD;</sup> cm at 10 Hz with a TGS target 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × 0.010 mm. The discussion will concern possible improvements concerning: (1) choice of material, and (2) crystal thickness, possibility of epitaxial growth.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Cyclotron Resonance in Metals
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This paper will deal with a comparison between Azbel'-Kaner cyclotron resonance performed at microwave frequencies and at far infrared frequencies, with emphasis on recent work in copper. The microwave measurements were performed at 73 GHz in the laboratory of Dr. C.C. Grimes and the far infrared measurements on two spectrometers of different designs: a reflection cavity spectrometer at the Bell Telephone Laboratories, Murray Hill, New Jersey, and a calorimetric spectrometer at Harvard University. The reflection cavity spectrometer shown in Fig. 1 employs a double Michelson interferometer where the two arms of the interferometer constitute a balanced bridge. A reflection cavity is placed in one arm of the interferometer which is tuned so that changes in the cavity reflectivity due to changes in the surface impedance of the sample will unbalance the signals at the two cooled germanium detectors of the bridge. The cavity, shown in Fig. 2, is bounded by a curved 1000-line/in. copper screen and the sample surface, and possesses a Q such that changes in reflectivity of the cavity are 100 times as large as would be seen from the bare metal sample.

articleTitle: A Microwave Biased Submillimeter GaAs Photodetector
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Studies were mde of two different GaAs submillimeter detection systems. DC biased and microwave biased GaAs photoconductive detectors were compared and evaluated. The microwave biased detector exhibited a significantly wider bandwidth over that of the DC device.

articleTitle: Photoconductive Far Infrared Detection in Silicon
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A new type of far infrared detector is described with a useful long wavelength limit of about 400 μm. Fast response times of several microseconds (source limited) have been demonstrated with pulsed far infrared molecular laser detection.

articleTitle: Optically Pumped Far Infrared Lasers
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Intense superradiant laser action on a pure rotational transition in optically pumped CH3F has been recently reported. 1,2 It is the purpose of this paper to present a parametric study on similar superradiant transitions observed in other molecules.

articleTitle: Alfven Wave Transmission Study of Bismuth in the Far Infrared
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Absorption spectra of transmitted Alfven waves in bismuth in Faraday configuration and H directed at and near the bisectrix axis have been studied using the 311 and 337 μm radiation from a HCN laser and magnetic fields up to 100 kG.

articleTitle: Measurements of the Coslic Background in the 7–10 CM−1 Atmospheric Window
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We have measured the sky temperature trough the 7-10cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> atmospheric window from the Alpine station of Testa Grigia(3500m. a.s.l.). An upper limit of 2.7°K has been found.

articleTitle: Josephson Junction Bolometer
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A bolometer for use in the submillimeter and far infrared is described. The temperature sensitive element is an SNS Josephson junction. The electrical NEP is 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−15</sup> W/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> and the detectivity, D∗, is 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup> W<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Generation by Noncollinear Difference Frequency Mixing
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: New developments in far infrared generation by noncollinear mixing of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> lasers in GaAs and CdTe are presented. In particular, new folded crystal geometries which can yield orders of magnitude increase in the output power are discussed.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Spectroradiometers with n-InSb Detectors
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The optimal characteristics of amplitude splitters for submillimeter radiation beams are determined. Versions of optical schemes with large light gathering power utilized such splitters are proposed. Using them high sensitive reciving devices for 2-0.2 mm waveband region with Fabry-Perot and Michelson interferometers and n-InSb immersion detectors (spectroradiometers) are constructed.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Absorption Spectra amd Phase Transition of Indirect Excitons in Germanium
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The results are presented of the detailed studies on the exciton absorption spectra in ultrapure Ge in the spectrum region 0.67–1.1 and 1.7–3.7 mev with a backward-wave tube radiation. It is shown that the measured spectrum corresponds to the exciton's transitions from the ground to excited states. As a result of themperature measurements at 1.6–4.2°K the phase transition of excitons into condensed state has been observed without the formation of excitonic molecules.

articleTitle: “Group Theory of Submillimeterwave-Frequency Angular Correlation Functions Related to the Rotation of Molecules in Liquids”
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The group theory of submillimeterwave-frequency angular auto-correlation functions of almost-rigid polyatomic molecules in liquids is presented and illustrated by functions determined from vibration -rotation spectra.

articleTitle: Criteria for the Observation of Dicke Superradiance in the Submillimeter Wavelength Region
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The phenomena of Dicke superradiance is discussed from the standpoint of the Fokker-Planck differential equation representation derived from the master equation in the atomic coherent states. Results calculated from the solution of this equation together with a self-consistency argument first put forth by Arecchi and Courtens are used to present characteristics of and criteria for its detection.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Reflectivity and Electron Scattering in GaAs
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The reflectivity of n-GaAs has been measured between 16 and 230 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> by Fourier transform spectroscopy. The reflectivity is shown to be relatively independent of the electron scattering model and useful for determining carrier concentration and mobility.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Optical Properties of Free Holes in Tellurium
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The nonlinear optical properties due to mobile carriers in nonparabolic energy bands have been first proposed by Butcher and McLean and Lax et al, observed by Patel et a1 and described by Wolff and Pearson. All theories of this effect have used expansion of nonlinear currents in powers of the electric field of the wave.

articleTitle: Submillimetric Spectrometry using a Polarising Interferometer
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Two-beam interferometric spectrometry, in which a spectrum is obtained by taking the Fourier transform of an interferogram, is now the preferred technique for most applications in the submillimetre spectrum, say 5-200cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. The method most commonly in use is based on the Michelson or Twyman-Green configuration with a stretched dielectric film as beam-divider. The results obtained in practice using this method fall well short of what should be possible ideally. We have previously reported briefly on a new method of interferometry involving a polarising beam divider (ref.1). This has brought performances closer to the ideal. Examples of performance and a fuller discussion of the method are given in this paper.

articleTitle: High Pressure Far Infrared Spectroscopy of Ionic Solids
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A high pressure far infrared cell operating to truly hydrostatic pressures of 8 Kbars is described and used to determine the anharmonic self-energies associated with the q ≈ 0 transverse optic modes of ionic solids.

articleTitle: A Calibrated Experimental 20 μ Photometer
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A photometer has been built, calibrated and tested for photometry in the 20 μ atmospheric window. The spectral band is selected by means of four successive reflections at Irtran-1 crystal-material, fitted in a helium dewar together with a germanium bolometer. A reflective, near-focal-plane chopper modulates the beam in a square wave mode. The laboratory calibration showed a sensitivity of 3.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">eff</inf>/W corresponding with an efficiency of the photometer of 13%. Coupled to the 60 cm f/15 telescope in Roden a detection limit of 2.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−24</sup> W/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Hz could be established.

articleTitle: Pulse Control Unit for Repetitive, Slow Scan Far Infrared Interferometry
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An inexpensive electronic interface which controls the flow of a phase-detected signal from a Michelson interferometer to a signal averager is described. This interface is designed to add the advantages of signal averaging techniques to an existing slow scan interferometer system which employs phase sensitive detection and time constant averaging.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Commercial Fourier Spectrometers for the Submillimeter Wavelength Region
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The purpose of this paper will be to describe the current state-of-the-art of commercial interferometric Fourier spectroscopy, with particular reference to two recently developed Michelson interferometer systems, the POLYTEC FIR 30 and MIR 30, the operating characteristics of which are summarized in Table 1.

articleTitle: Balloon-Based Measurements of the Cosmic Background Radiation
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We have developed and flown a balloon-borne liquid helium cooled spectrometer to measure the cosmic background radiation in the 3-18 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> region. It features a cooled horn antenna, polarizing Michelson interferometer and germanium bolometer. These design features and the performance of the instrument are discussed.

articleTitle: Continuously Tunable Submillimeter Source by Difference Frequency Mixing in InSb of Spin-Flip Raman Lasers
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A strong resonant nonlinearity due to the conduction spins has been observed when the frequency (∼100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) of far-infrared (FIR), generated by difference frequency mixing of two orthogonally polarized CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser beams is tuned to the spin-resonance frequency in InSb.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> This effect has been used to generate submillimeter radiation<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> continuously tunable between 90-110 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> by difference frequency mixing the 944.2 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> pump and the magnetically tunable, frequency shifted Stokes radiation from an InSb spin flip Raman laser (SFR). Mixing occurs in a separate crystal of InSb. Since the Raman shift of the SFR is exactly equal to the spin resonance frequency the resonance condition is automatically achieved if the oscillator crystal and the mixer crystal are mounted in the same magnetic field (Fig. 1). In principle the functions could be combined and the SFR would then itself become a generator of continuously tunable submillimeter radiation. A separate mixer crystal has been used to simplify phase matching of the three frequency mixing process. Due to presence of multiple longitudinal modes of SFR laser, the frequency of FIR was not continuously tunable. An attempt to resolve this problem by using a nonresonant superradiant spin-flip Raman laser (NRSSFR) has been successful.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> Another way to obtain the FIR continuously tunable and also in cw operation is to use the ∼2.3μ radiation from CO laser as pump frequency.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4,5</sup> Work is in progress to overcome the phase-matching problem resulting from the large dispersion of refractive indices in the 5.3μ region.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>

articleTitle: Tunable Far Infrared Methyl Fluoride Laser using Transverse Optical Pumping
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Some severe limitations of optically-pumped superradiant FIR lasers (700 MHz line width, ragged pulse shape) may be overcome using transverse optical pumping (TOP). Strong (∼ 500 W) lines have been produced in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F with linewidth < 30 MHz, and cavity tuning has been achieved over a range of 460 MHz at 496 pan.

articleTitle: A Submillimeter Michelson Interferometer with Frustrated-Total-Internal-Reflection Beamsplitter
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An efficient beamsplitter for a Michelson interferometer can be made from a pair of 90° prisms, using the process of frustrated total internal reflection. The design, laboratory tests, and astronomical applications of such an interferometer are discussed.

articleTitle: Antiferromagnetic Resonance in NiO:Co2+ and NiO:Fe2+
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The antiferromagnetic resonance (AFMR) of NiO doped with Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> was studied at 4. 2 K in the far infrared spectral region by means of Fourier transform spectroscopy. For the Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> doped crystals, a strong shift of the AFMR line was observed. In case of the Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> doped crystal, this shift was much smaller. In addition, a second absorption line was found for larger concentrations of Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> (5 % to 7 %). All these effects are attributed to the single ion anisotropics of the Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> and Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> ions, and the experimental results are interpreted by means of a simple model calculation.

articleTitle: A Tunable Josephson Junction Far Infrared Source
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: We have studied radiation emitted by Nb-Nb point contact Josephson junctions at frequencies up to 30 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. Spectroscopic measurements on solids have been made using this source.

articleTitle: Far-Infrared Spectrum of Single Crystals of an Enzyme
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Far-infrared absorption spectrum of single crystals of lysozyme was measured between 10-500 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> at room and the liquid N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> temperatures. A number of absorption bands were observed, some of which were assigned to the main and the side chain vibrations of lysozyme.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Spectroscopy of Weak Antiferromagnets in Magnetic Fields up to 300 kOe
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Antiferromagnetic resonance (AFMR) in weak antiferromagnets (WF) is investigated at wavelength λ = 300μ-14mm at 4.2-400°K in magnetic fields (MF) up to 300kOe. A new theoretical approach to the physics of magnetic fenomena is developed.

articleTitle: Submillimeter EPR Spectrum of Fe3+ in Hemoglobin
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The zero field splitting of the high spin ferric ion in a frozen solution of methemoglobin is obtained from the frequency dependence of the g-value determined by EPR experiments performed in the wavelength range: 4-0.7mm. The submillimeter EPR spectrometer and the results are described.

articleTitle: Development and Application of Optically Pumped Submillimeter Lasers
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Submillimeter lasers are optically pumped far from molecular absorptions using high power pumping or Stark tuning. Lasing between vibrational levels has been demonstrated with overtone pumping. These lasers have been applied to solid state spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Interferometry at 337 μ on a Tokamak Plasma
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The ALCATOR electron density (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">13</sup> < n < 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">14</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>) has been measured with a 337μ Mach-Zender interferometer. A detailed description of the interferometer is given. Results are discussed and compared with microwave interferometry data.

articleTitle: A Black Body Reference Standard for the Submillimetre Spectrum
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A reflection interference filter is used as an absorber in a new type of Black Body cavity for use as a standard source for the submillimetre spectrun. An emissivity of better than 99.9% is obtained and the effective temperature is well defined.

articleTitle: “HCN-Laser Diagnostics”
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Diagnostics of the cw-HCN-laser plasma with field and temperature probe, a mass spectrometer, as well as related exoeriments prove that H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> or D<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> molecules are required as collision partners of the HCN molecules. The formation of laser-active HCN molecules on the tube wall influence the radial gain profile. With this effect the excitation or suppression of higher HCN-laser modes can be controlled by the chemical composition of the laser gas.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Emission from a Tokamak Plasma near the Electron Cyclotron Frequency
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An experiment is described in which the emission from a tokamak plasma in the region of the electron cyclotron frequency and its low harmonics (up to the sixth) is measured. The results are compared with the predictions of the theory of cyclotron emission.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Voltage-Tunable Spectrometer-Detector
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An n-channel MOSFET at low temperatures exhibits a photoresistive response when illuminated by far-infrared radiation due to electron transitions defined by the potential at the Si-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> interface. Gate voltage variations lead to continuous tuning between 8 and 35 meV.

articleTitle: Application of a Far Infrared Grille Spectrometer to the Study of Methyl Cyanide Vapor near 360 cm−1
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A grille spectrometer vas specially adapted to the spectral range 20–45 μm. This apparatus, combining the properties of high resolution and large throughput, allowed us to achieve the analysis of the γ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sub> vibration-rotation band of methyl cyanide near 360 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. The molecular constants are in good agreement with those provided by microwave measurements.

articleTitle: “Construction and Performance of a Transversely Excited 337 μm-HCN-Laser”
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The transversely excited 337 μm-HCN-laser with an output power near 1 kW is described. Relevant data on the construction, laser-gases and performance are presented.

articleTitle: Development of MW-Level, Narrow-Band, FIR Lasers for Plasma Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Required MW-level, 30 MHz linewidth, 496 μm radiation for plasma diagnostics may be achieved in CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>F using an oscillator-pulse amplifier combination employing transverse optical pumping (TOP). It is estimated that an upper limit of 150 joules of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser pump energy is required to produce 1 MW (.07 joules, 60 nsec) FIR pulses.

articleTitle: Airborne Solar and Stratospheric Submilltmeter Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A high resolution Michelson interferometer has been used to obtain solar spectra from a jet aircraft in the low stratosphere. The spectra are absolutely calibrated in intensity, enabling the solar brightness temperature to be specified from 200 to 700 p. Concentrations of trace gases in the stratosphere are determined from intensity of absorption lines.

articleTitle: Plasma Effects in the HCN Laser
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Plasma conditions in the pulsed HCN laser are critical to its performance. The radial electron distribution is such as to produce strong focusing initially. A magnetic field can be used to enhance or reduce or modulate the output.

articleTitle: Attenuation of Submillimeter Radiation by Clouds and Rain
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The scattering and extinction properties of cloud and rain elements for far-infrared and submillimeter radiation have been estimated on the basis of recently determined optical constants, by means of polydisperse Mie scattering theory and realistic drop-size distributions.

articleTitle: Characterization and Ultimate Performance of Compensated n-Type Silicon Bolometer Detectors at Liquid Helium Temperatures
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The dependence of the resistivity and FIR absorptance on donor concentration, compensation, and temperature in compensated n-type Si is reported. The effect of environment, time-constant, and spectral-passband on the NEP of the compensated Si bolometer is examined and compared with similar calculations for the compensated Ge bolometer.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Heterodyne Detection and Harmonic Mixing using Schottky Diodes
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Schottky diodes have been used for submillimeter heterodyne detection and harmonic mixing. In particular, extremely sensitive detectors of optically pumped lasers have been demonstrated using a carcinotron local oscillator at 890μ.

articleTitle: Optically Pumped Submillimeter Wave Sources
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Optical pumping of polar molecules by means of an infrared laser has lead to the discovery of about 280 new laser lines between 34 micrometers and 1.8 mm. Very stable cw operation, very high pulsed output, and many other advantages over discharge excitation are offered.

articleTitle: Cyclotron Resonance at High Frequency in Metals
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An original spectrometer permits the observation of cyclotron resonance in metals in the 2-0. 6mm wavelength band. Physical results concern the electron-phonon interaction in lead and indium, and the Fermi surface of a ferromagnetic metal, nickel.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Noise in the far Infrared
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Noise measuraments in the frequency region 6.5×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−5</sup> - 1.6×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> Hz and 5-200 Hz have been performed between 300 and 3000 microns at the observatory of Testa Grigia (3500 m.a.s.l.). During clear and dry days and ninths no excess of noise has been detected with respect to the photon noise of a 300°K blackbody.

articleTitle: Surface Channel Detection of Millimeter Waves in InSb
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A new detector in the millimeter wave region of the spectrum has been developed using heavily doped but closely compensated InSb. Conduction in this detector is along a surface channel and detectors have been constructed with responsivities at peak of 500 V/Watt and an NEP at peak of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−10</sup> Watts/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>.

articleTitle: Experiments on Josephson Mixers for Heterodyne Reception at 0.3 mm Wavelength
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A point contact Josephson junction has been investigated as a heterodyne mixer at 337 μm. The conversion efficiency reached about -32 dB using a laser local oscillator and about -42 dB using 9th or 12th harmonic mixing with a klystron.

articleTitle: Submillimeter-Laser Magnetospectroscopy in Tellurium Making Use of the Nernst Effect
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: In contrast to magneto-transmission and magneto-photoconductivity measurements in tellurium the radiation induced Nernst effect reveals impurity and cyclotron transitions exactly and is not obscured by other effects as demonstrated in samples of different dislocation densities.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Optical Properties of Selenium and Cadmium Telluride
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The submillimeter region is an area of the spectrum where a limited knowledge of the linear optical properties of useful materials exists. Trigonal (class 32) Se and cubic (class 43m) CdTe have important linear and nonlinear optical properties in the near infrared for laser optics.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,2</sup> To extend their usefulness, the optical constants (index of refraction n and power absorption α = 4Πk/λ) of Se and CdTe have been measured in the 10 to 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup> range. Fourier transform spectroscopy, combined with the channeled spectrum technique, provided a convenient method of obtaining accurate far-IR optical data. These data have been combined with the available data from the literature to obtain a new and improved oscillator fit and to obtain more accurate values for the fundamental lattice vibrations.

articleTitle: Tunable Far Ir Source via Difference Frequency Mixing in a Planar Dielectric Waveguide
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Discretely tunable far infrared signals in the 100-1000 μm wavelength range, generated by phase matched difference frequency mixing selected pulsed CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser lines in a GaAs planar dielectric waveguide, are described. About 0.25 milliwatt (∼ 4.6% of theoretical) maximum with a 30% bandwidth tunability around 250 μm was achieved using a 4.87 mm length waveguide.

articleTitle: Josephson Junctions as Heterodyne Detectors
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Heterodyne detection with a point contact Josephson junction has been investigated both experimentally and theoretically. From our results at 36 GHz, we can extrapolate a potentially impressive performance for these devices at submillimeter wavelengths.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Radiation from Intense Relativistic Electron Beams
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Radiation from an intense relativistic electron beam at submillimeter wavelengths has been measured with bandpass and high-pass filters. Radiated power ∼ 100 kW has been measured in the passband 390 μm −540 μm. The generation of this radiation depends on giving the electrons a large energy component transverse to the magnetic guide field. Coherent wave generation mechanisms which may account for the observed radiation are discussed.

articleTitle: “Submillimeter-Wave Spectral Thermal Emission of Small Crystals and Thin Films of Alkalihalides”
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The submillimeterwave spectral emission of small crystals and thin films of alkalihalides was measured for different angles of emission and polarization. The resulting spectra are interpreted as virtual modes.

articleTitle: Assignments of Optically Pumped Laser Lines of 1,1-Difluorethylene
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The submillimetre laser transitions of CF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> have been assigned to pure rotation transitions in the v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>, v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> + v<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> vibrational states using results from laser Stark spectroscopy.

articleTitle: “The Influence of the Coriolis Coupling on Submillimeterwave-Frequency Angular Correlation Functions Related to the Rotation of Molecules in Liquids and Gases”
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The influence of Coriolis coupling on submillimeterwave-frequency angular auto-correlation functions describing the random rotation of spherical or symmetric molecules is calculated. Theoretical and experimental correlation functions of molecules with Coriolis effects are compared.

articleTitle: Far Infra-Red Properties of Interacting Donors in Antimony Doped Germanium
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Absorption and photoconductivity of 337 μm radiation in Sb-doped Ge have been investigated at liquid He temperatures; the result suggests that a delocalized excited state exists between the conduction band and the donor ground state.

articleTitle: Fourier Spectroscopy of Water Vapour in a Long Path Absorption Cell for the Range 5 cm−1 – 20 cm−1 (150 GHz to 600 GHz)
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Anomalous absorption, i.e. that not attributable to water monomer or oxygen has been detected in many atmospheric observations both slant path using the sun as source (ref. 1) and horizontal path using an artificial source (ref. 2). In the real atmosphere it is difficult to achieve adequate stability and homogenity in the path to find the true dependence of the anomalous absorption on temperature and relative humidity. This can be done better in laboratory conditions but long path lengths are necessary to get adequate absorption.

articleTitle: Interference Filters for Submillimeter Space Projects
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: High quality low-frequency pass and band pass metalic mesh interference filters are discussed, which cover the range 50μm to 1000μm. The use of these filters in satellite radiometry (operational) and balloon-borne astronomy is specifically considered.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Wave Generation and Amplification using Optical Pumping
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: An analysis of the performance of an optically pumped quantum paramagnetic amplifier/generator for submillimeter wave operation is given.

articleTitle: The Performance of an Amplitude Fourier Spectrometer for Far-Infrared Solid State Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A far-infrared Fourier interferometer for amplitude-phase reflection spectroscopy on solids is described. It can be used with small samples at low temperatures and with fairly high resolution (< 0.1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>). The spectral range presently is 10-1000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>.

articleTitle: A Cooled Interferometric Modulator to Measure the Cosmic Background Spectrum
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The experiment is designed to determine the spectrum of the cosmic background radiation in the wavelength range 3mm to 300μm., using a balloon-borne liquid helium cooled polarising interferometer with two indium antimonide detectors.

articleTitle: Far Infrared — Submillimeter Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The concept of a phased array of far infrared or submillimeter waveguide lasers that can be scanned electronically is presented. Grating lobe reduction by computer analysis is shown. The application in a low angle track-while-scan radar is discussed.

articleTitle: Recombination Radiation from Landau States in Impact Ionized GaAs
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Recombination radiation from Landau states in impact ionized high-purity GaAs has been observed. The narrow band (∼ 3 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>) emission has been magnetically tuned from 80 to 120 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>, and used to observe rotational transitions in water vapor.

articleTitle: Dispersive Reflection Spectroscopy in the Far Infrared by Division of the Field of View in a Michelson Interferometer
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A new technique, suitable for use at low temperatures and on relatively small samples, is described for measuring the amplitude and phase reflection spectra of solids in the far infrared without mechanical replacement of reflecting surfaces.

articleTitle: Tunable Far-Infrared Source Based on Radiative Transitions between Landau-Levels in N-Type InSb
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The radiative emission from impact ionized shallow donors in n-type InSb provides a tunable far-infrared source, the properties and applications of which are investigated. To obtain optimum conditions the radiation intensity is studied in dependence of the sample volume and the electric and magnetic field intensities. The source is applied to measure the Zeeman-splitting of the shallow donors in n-InP and n-G-aAs.

articleTitle: Evidence for 1.6 mm Wavelength Parametric Amplification in a Josephson Junction Microwave Source
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A Josephson junction 1.6 mm wavelength microwave source has been used to demonstrate the parametric amplification by reflection necessary to maintain parametric oscillations at 1.6 mm wavelength. A perturbation calculation based on the resistively and capacitively shunted Josephson junction model gives a negative effective microwave resistance for a junction biased at voltages higher than the voltage for a cavity induced step. The parametric oscillation was observed at voltages consistent with the region in which negative resistance was calculated.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Dielectric Processes in Liquids
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Recent advances in dispersive Fourier spectrometry are described. The complex refractive indices of lossy materials are now directly measurable over a wide spectral range and results overlapping with high-frequency microwave data will be presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Submillimeter and Millimeter Antiferromagnetic Resonance in Polycrystalline Nickel Oxide
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: The temperature dependence of the effective internal fields of NiO has been determined from antiferromagnetic resonance experiments at submillimeter frequencies using Fourier transform spectroscopy and at millimeter wavelengths with the usual spectroscopic techniques.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Magneto-Spectroscopy in n-Type InAs Epitaxial Layers: Shallow Hydrogenic Donor Impurity States
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Submillimeter magneto-spectroscopic measurements of the shallow donor impurity in InAs epi-layer crystals have been made at low temperatures. Several excited state transitions have been observed for the first time, together with various transitions from the ground state.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Excitations in Antiferromagnetic Tungstates (NiWO4, CoWO4)
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Transition metal tungstates have a low symmetry crystalline lattice (spase group C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2h</inf>). They have biaxial antiferromagnetic structure below the Neel temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>=67°K for NiWO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> =55°K for CoWO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>). The ground state spin of a magnetic ion in these crystals is S > 1 (for Ni<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> S=1, for Co<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup> S=3/2). In this case we should expect both specific features of the AFMR mode behaviour in an applied magnetic field as temperature changes and new magnetic branches of the spin-wave<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1,2</sup>. The experiment was carried out diffraction spectrometer in linearly polarized radiation.

articleTitle: Interaction of Intense Submillimeter Radiation with Plasmas
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Recently developed high-power submillimeter lasers offer new possibilities for fundamental studies of laser-plasma and laser-solid interactions and may also be very useful in tokamak plasma diagnostics.

articleTitle: A Technique to Measure Submillimeter Tokomak Synchrotron Radiation Spectra
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: A wire mesh Fabry-Pérot interferometer with millisecond response time has been constructed. The application of this instrument to study the millimeter and submillimeter synchrotron radiation emitted by magnetically confined Tokamak plasmas is discussed.

articleTitle: Conference Committee
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: Provides a listing of current committee members and society officers.

articleTitle: Foreword
publicationTitle: 1974 International Conference on Submillimeter Waves and Their Applications
abstract: This is the first international conference on the general subject of submillimeter waves and their applications. We expect it to be the first of a long series because the submillimeter wave specialty has become well-defined and moderately well populated. It is clear from our experience during the past ten years that we can expect at least one outstanding advance every two or three years in the science, technology. and/or application of submillimeter waves. This conference will reveal several as well as many needed improvements in the technology and applications.
